symptoms: Tiny pale spots appear first on the underside of young open leaves.
Spots grow into brown streaks that run along the leaf veins.
Streaks darken, turn black and become oval patches.
Badly hit leaves become blackened and water-soaked, then dry out.
Leaf loss reduces the green leaves the plant needs to fill bunches.
entries.look_alikes: Yellow Sigatoka: young streaks have a clear yellow halo, which black Sigatoka lacks, and it develops more slowly.
cultural_actions: Remove infected leaves from the plantation regularly.
Keep the field well drained to reduce humidity.
Avoid close planting so leaves dry quickly.
Keep the field weed free.

treatment_options.active_ingredient: Petroleum (banana spray) oil mixed with fungicide

entries.when_to_act: TNAU lists Sigatoka sprays as a rotation of fungicides with oil; see your KVK for the local spray timing and green-leaf target.

symptoms: Pale yellow or greenish streaks appear parallel to the leaf veins.
Streaks turn into oval brown spots.
Spot centre turns light grey with a yellow ring around it.
Spots join to form large dried patches on the leaf.
Leaves dry fast and fall, so bunches may not fill well.
entries.look_alikes: Black Sigatoka: streaks turn black and lack the yellow halo, and it spreads faster.
cultural_actions: Remove and destroy affected leaves.
Keep the field weed free and remove suckers on time.
Avoid close spacing when planting.
Provide good drainage and prevent waterlogging.
entries.when_to_act: TNAU: start sprays when the first leaf specks appear, and repeat at the interval on the label or your KVK advice.

entries.cause: Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense (soil-borne fungus)
symptoms: Lower and oldest leaves turn yellow and wilt.
Leaf edges dry and the plant looks spiky.
Yellow to reddish streaks show along the pseudostem.
Cut rhizome shows reddish-brown to maroon discolouration in a circle.
Plant collapses as the disease advances.
entries.look_alikes: Moko (bacterial wilt): youngest leaves yellow first and a greyish-brown slimy ooze comes from cut stems.
cultural_actions: Plant healthy suckers and avoid injuring roots.
Rotate with paddy or sugarcane before replanting banana.
Remove diseased plants with the soil around them.
Choose varieties TNAU lists as tolerant; avoid very susceptible ones.
Keep good drainage, balanced feeding and weed control.
entries.when_to_act: TNAU stresses prevention: treat suckers before planting and apply bio-agents at planting and later stages as per label or KVK advice.

Remove infected plants early.
Disinfect pruning tools between plants.

Use basin irrigation, not furrow irrigation.

entries.cause: Banana bract mosaic virus (a potyvirus), spread by aphids and infected suckers
symptoms: Spindle-shaped pink to reddish streaks appear on pseudostem, midrib and bunch stalk.
Mosaic streaks show on bracts and fingers.
New suckers show reddish-brown streaks.
Leaves cluster at the crown like a traveller's palm.
Bunch stalk is long and the hands are half filled.
entries.look_alikes: Banana bunchy top: dark green streaks along veins and narrow, bunched leaves. Cucumber mosaic: yellow mosaic bands on leaves.
cultural_actions: Use virus-free planting material, such as tested tissue culture plants.
Remove diseased plants at once.
Keep the garden and nearby area free of weeds.
Inspect the field often for early signs.
Control aphids that carry the virus.

treatment_options.active_ingredient: Neemkosol (neem-based product) for aphid vector control
treatment_options.note: Vector control only; FOLLOW PRODUCT LABEL; no dose

entries.when_to_act: No cure for infected plants. Remove them early; see your KVK for aphid control timing.

entries.cause: Several insects attack banana; TNAU lists corm weevil, pseudostem borer, banana aphid, thrips, leaf-eating caterpillars and flea beetles
symptoms: Identify the insect first, as each pest needs different action.
Corm weevil: yellowing leaves and tunnels in the corm.
Pseudostem borer: jelly-like ooze and holes on the stem.
Aphids: sticky honeydew, curled dwarf leaves.
Thrips and beetles scar the fruit skin and tender leaves.
entries.look_alikes: Damage can look like disease. Aphid spread viruses such as bunchy top and bract mosaic; check for virus signs.
cultural_actions: Use clean, pest-free suckers or tissue culture plants.
Remove dried leaves and old stumps, and keep the field clean.
Uproot and burn badly infested plants.
Use pheromone and split-stem traps for weevils.
Keep weeds down.
entries.when_to_act: Spray only after you identify the insect; see your KVK for local thresholds and timing.

entries.cause: Small sap-sucking insects (order Hemiptera, family Aphididae), e.g. Aphis gossypii, Aphis craccivora, Myzus persicae, Pentalonia nigronervosa
symptoms: Small soft-bodied insects, green, yellowish, brown or black, sit on tender shoots and leaf undersides.
Nymphs and adults suck sap, so leaves curl, crinkle and look pale.
Plants become stunted.
Sticky honeydew attracts black sooty mould.
Some aphids spread plant viruses.
entries.look_alikes: Whiteflies and thrips also cause curling; aphids are soft, wingless or winged, with two small tubes at the rear.
cultural_actions: Scout tender shoots and leaf undersides regularly.
Use yellow sticky traps to track winged aphids.
Use clean planting material and keep weeds down.
Protect ladybird beetles, lacewings and parasitoids; TNAU lists them for banana aphid.
Remove virus-infected plants before spraying.
entries.when_to_act: TNAU pages opened give no threshold; see your KVK for the local threshold and spray only if needed.

Leaves crinkle and curl upward, with yellow or silvery streaks.

entries.cause: Sap-sucking insects (family Cicadellidae), e.g. Amrasca biguttula on cotton and sunflower, rice green leafhopper Nephotettix virescens
symptoms: Small green, wedge-shaped insects that walk sideways on the leaf.

Keep fields weed free and sow on time together.
Place rice nurseries away from street lamps.
Use light traps and resistant rice varieties, as TNAU suggests.
Scout leaf undersides regularly.

Choose resistant or straight-leaved varieties where available.
Ensure good ventilation and adequate watering.
Scout leaf undersides regularly with a hand lens.

entries.cause: Small jumping leaf beetles (Coleoptera, Chrysomelidae, Alticinae), e.g. striped flea beetle Phyllotreta striolata; banana flea beetles Nodostoma and Colapsis
symptoms: Small beetles that hop when disturbed.
Adults chew many tiny round holes in leaves, called shot-holes.
On banana, they scratch tender leaves and scar the fruit skin.
Grubs of some species feed on roots, causing grooves and poor growth.
entries.look_alikes: Caterpillar damage makes larger ragged holes; flea beetle holes are small and round.
cultural_actions: Do deep summer ploughing to expose overwintering adults.
Use well-decomposed farmyard manure and neem cake before sowing.
Control weeds with timely intercultural operations.
Grow sorghum or maize border rows or mustard trap crop.
Use yellow sticky traps for monitoring.

treatment_options.note: Listed as a last resort; FOLLOW PRODUCT LABEL; no dose

entries.when_to_act: See your KVK for the local threshold; the opened sources give none.
